theSpecimenCauseNumberQuestion.whatIsPrinted: 'No.: TEST-2026-000001' in the caption of the Article 994 motion (page 1) and the Article 995 order (page 4) on the canonical fixture, and 'No.: TEST-BOUNDARY-2026-0000000000000001' in the same two places on the boundary fixture. theSpecimenCauseNumberQuestion.verdict: ACCEPTABLE ON THESE BYTES, and FIX142 was right not to touch it.
why: It is not a specimen the build invented. It is the value of case.docket_number in the canonical FIXTURE record, sitting alongside 'Jordan Avery Reyes', '1991-04-17', 'Tangipahoa Parish' and 'Division A'. In production that slot carries the docket number the participant supplies. Marking this one value as a specimen while leaving the fixture name, DOB, parish and division unmarked would state something false about which of them is real.

The fixture-ness of the artifact is carried where a reader can actually rely on it, not by a page watermark: the PDF Title is 'Interim Motion to Expunge a Felony Arrest from Criminal History (La. C.Cr.P. art. 985.1) - canonical', and build-status.json reads generationAllowed false, runtimeSelectable false, commercialRoutesOpened 0, selfVerified false, independentVerificationStatus PENDING. No participant can be handed this file.

It is a cohort convention, not this family's choice. All seven Louisiana census-v1 families use exactly 'TEST-2026-000001' for canonical and 'TEST-BOUNDARY-2026-0000000000000001' for boundary. Changing it on one family would break the cohort's comparability without changing what any participant receives.
Changing it was also outside FIX142's grant and would have contradicted its own no-value-changed guarantee, which this lane verified: the nineteen declared writes are unchanged across the repair.
theSpecimenCauseNumberQuestion.theConditionOnThatAcceptance: It is acceptable BECAUSE the artifact is a fixture that no route can deliver. If any route is ever opened that renders this family for a real participant, the docket number must come from the participant record and the assertion that it does must be measured on the delivered bytes; a route that shipped these fixture bytes would be shipping a court caption bearing the word TEST, which is not acceptable on a page a clerk stamps.

theLabelStrippingExplanationIsWrong.test1: classifyField, run directly from scripts/rcap-packet-completeness/completeness-contract.mjs, returns the IDENTICAL result for both labels: 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle)' -> {id: UNMATCHED, requirement: UNKNOWN}, and 'Current legal name' -> {id: UNMATCHED, requirement: UNKNOWN}. The stripping made no difference to the classifier FIX142 names. It would have classified the full caption exactly as it classified the reduced one.
theLabelStrippingExplanationIsWrong.test2: No counter in the set is a value-versus-caption-format check. PASS_COUNTERS is knownRequiredFieldsMissing, requiredFactsNotCollected, unclassifiedBlanks, incompleteRows, requiredOptionsMissing, requiredComponentsMissing, invisibleWrites, protectedWrites, visualDefects. classifyBlank decides dispositions from a field's label class and its declared disposition; it never inspects the WRITTEN VALUE against a caption's stated order. With the name still written and the label un-stripped, all nine would still have read zero.
theLabelStrippingExplanationIsWrong.test3: The un-stripped caption would, if anything, have made the platform MORE confident about writing the assembled name in natural order, not less. captionAsksForEveryNamePart from scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs returns TRUE for 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle)' and FALSE for the stripped 'Current legal name' (verified live -- and note that passing it an object instead of a string makes it return false for everything, which is a trap this lane fell into once before correcting it). Its documented purpose is to make a caption that enumerates the parts resolve to participant.full_legal_name, the assembled whole. So on the full caption the platform's designed answer is: refuse first_name/last_name/middle_name and write full_legal_name -- in natural order.
theLabelStrippingExplanationIsWrong.theRealRootCause: captionAsksForEveryNamePart is ORDER-BLIND. It cannot distinguish 'Full Name (First, Middle, Last, Suffix)', where natural order is correct, from 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle)', where it is wrong. That is the hole, it lives in the shared semantics layer rather than in Hawaii's builder, and it will produce the same defect on any pinned form whose name caption specifies surname-first order. FIX142's repair is correct for this family and does not close that hole.
theLabelStrippingExplanationIsWrong.notARepairRequest: Recorded for the queue. VF43 changed no byte of rcap-field-semantics.mjs or of any other family.
